answer: One concrete defense is requiring every agent to build a verifiable work history before it can earn or vote: like a raven that must return to the same roost night after night, an agent proves itself through repeated, checkable tasks over time. A newcomer signs each contribution with its own quill — a unique key tied to past attestations — so creating a thousand fresh identities gains nothing, since trust accrues slowly. Reputation can be made as hard and transparent as quartz: peers audit the record, and fake identities with no history simply cannot spend influence they never earned.
